Give the code a clear place in the review.

CodeRabbit Change Stack · Product design take-home · Parth Pawar · October 19, 2026

A reviewer needs to know where they are, understand the change, and decide what to do next. This redesign keeps layer-based review while giving navigation, code, and explanations distinct roles.

Observed in the supplied screenDesign decision and expected benefit
Several toolbars compete with the diff.A compact PR header carries the final review action. One file toolbar holds diff layout, focus, and viewed status. Secondary tool placement is proposed in Tools; those workflows are not prototyped.
Layer and file navigation are separated.Expandable files live under their layer. The selected layer, file, and dependency remain visible together, reducing the need to reconstruct location.
Summaries are detached from their code ranges.Selecting a summary reveals and highlights its code. The same selection treatment connects explanation and evidence; additions and deletions retain their signs.
File completion and the review decision are easy to conflate.Mark viewed updates file progress only. Submit review opens a separate decision dialog. Focus mode preserves position while hiding surrounding panels.

Interaction proof

The working prototype demonstrates J/K navigation, summary-to-code selection, Unified/Split views, Z focus mode, reversible viewed status, a local comment draft, and simulated submission. Keyboard shortcuts are ignored while typing. At narrower desktop widths, context opens over the code rather than squeezing it further.

Evidence and limits

The supplied screenshots show coderabbitai/mono #22041, with two layers and three files. The linked live Formbricks PR is a different 52-file example and its public review checks were rate limited. This comparison therefore uses the screenshot’s visible file consistently. Code is transcribed with normalized wrapping; summaries are condensed. Missing code and original comment text are identified rather than reconstructed.

Validation covers desktop layout, keyboard behavior, progress, dialog focus, and recovery states. These checks establish prototype behavior; they do not measure reviewer speed or replace testing with developers. Review decisions and drafts remain in the browser tab and are never sent.
